calls.title: 30 min with Karen (Luke Sonnet)
calls.summary: The team is focusing on a new website strategy designed to target distinct user roles, beginning with data scientists. They have launched role-specific pages to meet unique user needs and plan to develop additional pages for data engineers and engineers. The content aims to highlight GrowthBook's scalability and its support for experimentation programs. Discussions emphasized audience segmentation, clarifying messaging for different roles, with a focus on integration, visualization, and addressing common pain points for data scientists. Contributions from participants, including Luke, Ashley, and Karen, highlighted the importance of trust, clarity, and effective messaging in refining the website content to facilitate user engagement.
calls.keywords: Data Scientist, Metrics Library, Statistical Rigor, Quantile Metrics, Experimentation Scaling, Deployment Options
calls.action_items:
**Karen Henke**
Refine the header messaging for the Data Science page to better reflect flexibility and control in experimentation while communicating scale (08:14)
Incorporate bullet points on advanced metric types—retention, ratio, quantile—in the benefits section with emphasis on customization and organizational standards (26:14)
Decide on the visuals and screenshots to highlight key benefits and statistical features on the Data Science page (09:17)
Maintain focus on the data scientist persona when finalizing the page content, keeping procurement and deployment details lower on the page (30:18)

**Luke Sonnet**
Share main metrics documentation page link with Karen for reference on advanced metrics content (26:07)
Provide possible blog or example content explaining quantile metrics for use in educational or marketing materials (22:19)

**Ashley Stirrup**
Add the creation of a data engineer-focused role page to the website revamp task list (05:53)
